summary: Confirmed DONE by commit 60633eff3 (#710). The standard web build writes .gz siblings for hashed assets, and the Ryco server (Node and Bun platforms, router route and early startup-gate route) negotiates Accept-Encoding against them. Responses carry Content-Encoding, Vary: Accept-Encoding, a per-variant weak ETag, the original Content-Type and a working 304 path, and nothing is compressed on the fly. I checked the local Oct 14 dist: all 691 compressible hashed assets of 1 KiB or more have a .gz (28,015 KiB raw, 8,137 KiB gz). The only hashed files without one are 4 .pfb fonts that fail the 10% saving rule. The CORS middleware merges Vary instead of replacing it. Icon overrides only touch unhashed top-level files, so no sibling goes stale. No relay or proxy path forwards static requests in a way that could double-decode. The deviations left are minor and deliberate: gzip by default with brotli opt-in, no HTTP/2 on the plain-HTTP server, and unhashed on-demand files (vscode-icons, index.html) are served as identity. None of these is on the cold-load path to the composer at meaningful size.

evidence.note: createPrecompressedAssetsPlugin() is registered only for the standard client mode. Desktop and the CLI node use this mode; the only other mode is hosted-hub.
HASHED_ASSET_PATTERN limits siblings to content-hashed names. Siblings can never go stale, and unhashed public files (index.html, vscode-icons) get none.
A sibling is written only if it saves at least 10%. This is why the hashed Foxit*.pfb fonts have no .gz in the dist.
Brotli is opt-in by design (comment: browsers send br only over HTTPS; avoids doubling package and artifact size). The server already prefers br whenever a .br exists.
writeBundle iterates the Rollup bundle. Worker outputs and the pdf.js .mjs are included, but files copied from public/ are not.

691 hashed assets have .gz siblings (28,015 KiB to 8,137 KiB). Without siblings: 4 hashed .pfb files (incompressible), index.html (4 KB), desktop-boot.html, mockServiceWorker.js, favicon.svg, and about 690 on-demand vscode-icons SVGs (3.4 MB raw in total, never loaded in bulk).
fs.copy(webDist, clientTarget) carries the siblings into dist/client. The local apps/server/dist/client/assets also has 691 .gz files.
staticFileEtag adds a -br/-gzip variant suffix. The stat comes from the served sibling.
acceptedStaticContentEncodings follows RFC 9110: q=0, * wildcard, x-gzip alias.

staticFileResponse: Vary is set for every precompressible extension. Siblings are stat-probed in parallel and the preferred one wins. Content-Type comes from the original path, and the 304 path drops Content-Encoding but keeps Vary. setHeaders overrides the platform's own ETag.
identityOnly applies only to desktop mode plus a loopback Host. LAN (desktop exposure bind 0.0.0.0) and Tailscale Serve clients of a desktop node still get gzip.
The early startup-gate static handler reuses serveStaticRequest, so it negotiates the same way.
The CORS preResponseHandler merges Origin into the existing Vary via varyWith, so Vary: Accept-Encoding is not clobbered on the CORS-wrapped static routes.

Integration tests cover br/gzip/identity selection, gzip-only builds for br-capable clients, identity for the desktop loopback renderer, and fallback without a sibling. http.test.ts:144-173 covers parsing and ETags.
The hosted surface is covered separately. The Hub image build precompresses br+gzip and negotiates (scripts/build-static-manifest.ts), which matches the hosted-hub exclusion in vite.config.
The desktop node can bind 0.0.0.0 for LAN exposure, so the .gz siblings shipped in the desktop artifact are not dead weight.

fixDefects:
No defect in the fix. Corrections and nits on the auditor's notes:
1. Auditor defect 3 is inaccurate. The .gz siblings in the desktop artifact are used: identityOnly (http.ts:910) skips them only for loopback Hosts, and a desktop node exposed on the LAN (serverExposure.ts bind 0.0.0.0) or via Tailscale Serve (which keeps the incoming Host) serves gzip to those remote browsers.
2. HTTP/2: browsers never do h2c, so h2 is only possible over TLS. The node has no TLS listener; the existing TLS path is Tailscale Serve's HTTPS frontend, which terminates TLS in front of the node. Proposal part 4 ('consider') therefore needs no Ryco-side change unless the node gains its own TLS listener.
3. Brotli off by default is a deliberate, documented trade-off. It costs about 15% more bytes (about 1853 vs 1566 KiB per cold load) only for HTTPS (Tailscale Serve) clients.
4. Unhashed on-demand files (public/vscode-icons, about 690 SVGs of 1 KiB or more, 3.4 MB in total, largest 248 KB; index.html 4 KB) are served as identity. They are not on the cold path to the composer.
Unrelated aside, outside this finding: resolveStaticCacheControl (http.ts:113) classifies some unhashed public files as immutable for a year, because their basenames are 8 or more [A-Za-z0-9_-] characters: mockServiceWorker.js, apple-touch-icon.png, favicon-96x96.png, web-app-manifest-*.png and every vscode-icons SVG. This predates the fix (same regex at f1be4abc7). desktop-boot.html matches too but is loaded through the desktop custom scheme, not HTTP.
implementationSketch:
Nothing is required. Optional follow-ups, in order of value:
(a) If HTTPS/Tailscale Serve access matters, call createPrecompressedAssetsPlugin({ brotli: true }) in apps/web/vite.config.ts:133. The server needs no change, because PRECOMPRESSED_ASSET_ENCODINGS already lists br first. Cost: about 6-7 MB more in the npm package and the desktop artifact, plus slower builds at quality 11. Check by extending buildPlugins.test.ts to expect .br, and curl against a Tailscale Serve URL with 'Accept-Encoding: br'.
(b) Precompress the versioned on-demand directory as well. In the plugin's closeBundle, walk outDir/vscode-icons/v*/ (ON_DEMAND_WEB_ASSET_DIRECTORIES in scripts/lib/onDemandWebAssets.ts) and run the same 1 KiB and 10% rules. The directory is version-pinned, so it is as immutable as a hash. The server already negotiates for any .svg that has a sibling. Add a buildPlugins.test.ts case.
(c) Separate item: tighten the resolveStaticCacheControl hash regex (http.ts:113) to Vite's '-<8 base64url>.<ext>' shape (the same as HASHED_ASSET_PATTERN; consider sharing it via @ryco/shared/precompressedAssets), so unhashed public files get no-cache. vscode-icons/v<version>/ can stay immutable through an explicit prefix rule. Add http.test.ts cases for mockServiceWorker.js, apple-touch-icon.png and favicon-96x96.png.
decisionReason: No decision is needed for the finding itself (DONE). Enabling brotli by default is a minor product trade-off (install and artifact size against about 15% fewer wire bytes for HTTPS clients only), already decided against in the code comment. It can be revisited without any security or protocol impact.
